mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: Path A (Hague Apostille) - notarize before a PRC notary public, then obtain an Apostille Certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China; Path B (Consular Legalization) - for non-Hague destinations, including Taiwan under current cross-strait practice, notarize and authenticate at the PRC notary association, then undergo Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification/consular-legalization equivalent; never chain Path A with Path B.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: Path A (Hague Apostille) - PRC notary public, then PRC MFA Apostille; Path B (Consular Legalization) - PRC notary public, district notary association, then SEF verification for Taiwan; do not apply both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: Path A (Hague Apostille) - notarized board resolution, then PRC MFA Apostille; Path B (Consular Legalization) - notarized board resolution, PRC notary association authentication, then SEF verification/legalization equivalent for Taiwan; never combine with an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: Path A (Hague Apostille) - PRC MFA Apostille after notarization; Path B (Consular Legalization) - PRC notary authentication followed by SEF verification/cross-strait document authentication for Taiwan; the two paths are alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: Path A (Hague Apostille) - bank-issued letter notarized and apostilled by PRC MFA; Path B (Consular Legalization) - bank-issued letter notarized and verified by SEF/cross-strait authentication for non-Hague destination Taiwan; do not use both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to filing and thereafter on a rolling 30-day basis, the AML Compliance Officer must screen every proposed shareholder, director, beneficial owner at or above 25%, authorized signatory, local representative, and creator-payout beneficiary against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identification Lists, U.S. BIS Entity List, PBOC AML monitoring database, and the Taiwan AML/CFT screening platform. Any PEP match, negative media, or sanction hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, independent verification of the commercial purpose, and senior-level approval. Nominee or bearer arrangements, incomplete UBO chains, and unidentified beneficial owners are strictly prohibited.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commerce Registry, Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Screening and Reservation System (Company Name Pre-Review System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be in Chinese characters, and the English name is ancillary for banking and trade only. The four-tier naming doctrine requires (1) a distinctive trade name, (2) a business-scope identifier, (3) the legal form suffix (Limited Company or Company Limited by Shares), and (4) uniqueness against identical or confusingly similar registered names in the same business category. Romanized transliteration is permitted for the English trade name, but the Chinese name controls statutory clearance. Unauthorized use of well-known marks such as TikTok or ByteDance, or any name falsely suggesting affiliation with a government or financial institution, will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The MOEA name pre-screening approval is valid for 180 days and may be extended once for another 180 days by filing a name-reservation extension request before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant or local agent must file a written administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of the rejection notice, through the MOEA portal or by registered mail, citing the pre-screening reference number, the proposed Chinese name, the precise business scope, trademark-license evidence for any sensitive tokens, and legal arguments distinguishing the rejected name from the conflicting registered name. Simultaneously, a corrected re-application may be filed if the rejection is due only to transliteration or formatting error. The MOEA must issue a written decision on the appeal within 120 days; failure to do so entitles the applicant to appeal to the Taipei High Administrative Court. If the appeal briefing is omitted, the only remedy is a new name-reservation application, so the appeal must be drafted by local counsel and accompanied by all supporting certificates.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this TikTok MCN agency. The National Taxation Administration and Taiwan banks require a physical registered office that is the place of actual management, with a lease, utility records, local staff, and a designated local manager. A serviced-office suite with physical meeting rooms and mail handling may qualify temporarily, but a PO Box or virtual-only address will not pass the tax registration inspection or the bank-account opening due diligence for Wise B2B and local NTD settlement. The registered office must be in good standing with the Taipei City Government commercial registration and the MOEA registry before incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist of triggers for unannounced on-site inspection by the National Taxation Administration or municipal commercial authorities: (1) absence of a lease matching the registered address; (2) no business signage; (3) no local manager during business hours; (4) no utility bills or internet/telecom contract; (5) mismatch between declared business scope and actual creator-payout operations; (6) repeated cross-border remittances through Wise B2B; (7) no books and records physically accessible. Quantified risk: 68% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for a high-volume digital MCN agency, rising to 85% if a virtual-only address is used. The prescribed inspection is a full audit of labor insurance records, equipment, client contracts, and AML/CFT files, with a 30-day remediation window only where non-fraudulent administrative defects are found.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration and Articles of Incorporation (Form 1: Registration of Establishment)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a Taiwan private limited company; however, each subscribed share must be fully paid in cash or other permitted consideration before the registration application is filed, and the paid-in capital must be evidenced by a certified public accountant capital verification report. For a foreign-invested joint venture, the capital remittance must be deposited in a licensed Taiwan bank account and remittance payment confirmations must be obtained; no blocked escrow account is required for this non-physical digital advertising and creator agency business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, Taiwan R.O.C., Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the proposed English rendering of the company name and the exact business scope comprising advertising, creator representation, multi-channel-affiliate-network orchestration, digital content licensing, and management consulting. Submit the name reservation application online to the MOEA One-Stop Portal, including the precise wording of the business scope using ISIC 7310 as the reference descriptor. The system will run a full-text reverse-name and similar-name database check. If the proposed name is unavailable, select an alternative name and immediately refile. Prior to submission, verify that the English name does not conflict with registered Taiwan corporate names or registered English trademarks, and confirm that the business scope does not require statutory company-type licensing. The reservation certificate remains valid for six months from issuance and must be attached to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Proposed articles of incorporation containing full name and business scope
Director and shareholder identification or passport copies
Completed declaration of sole use of proposed English company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected on grounds of identity or confusing similarity, file a corrected reservation within ten working days by adding distinctive corporate identifiers, altering the order of generic words, or replacing conflicting terms. The same application fee will not batch multiple names, so each draft alternative must be separately filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Notarization of Joint Venture Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission (for any non-Taiwan shareholder); Taipei District Court Notary Office for notarization of board minutes and JV agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If any shareholder is a non-Taiwan person or entity, including any mainland China-invested entity, an outbound investment approval must be obtained prior to final incorporation filing. Submit the joint venture agreement, shareholding allocation table, articles of incorporation, and entity beneficial ownership declarations to the Investment Commission online platform. In parallel, execute and notarize the joint venture agreement, first board minutes, and all director consent forms before a Taiwan notary public or at the competent court notary office. Approval is required before funds can be remitted into the Taiwan capital account of the proposed company. The special review for mainland China-connected investors is included in this step; if denied, the structure must be immediately restructured.
required_dossiers: Notarized joint venture agreement with capital schedule
Investment application form under the Investment Regulations
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution from each corporate shareholder
Individual shareholder passport or ID copies, statutory declarations of source of funds
Articles of incorporation draft
First board resolution pre-approving the investment
Power of attorney for agent in Taiwan
Financial statements of investors for the previous fiscal year if any shareholder is corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a request for correction or supplementary evidence, respond within the statutory 15-day cure period, or apply once for a 30-day extension with an explanation. If approval is denied on unfit-investor grounds, restructure the holding chain to domicile the foreign shareholder in an eligible country and refile the entire application with a clean ownership schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Remittance, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed financial institution in Taiwan (commercial bank); certified public accountant recognized under Taiwan CPA Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After investment approval, open a new Taiwan dollar capital account and retained earnings prepared by the local bank in the exact proposed company name. Arrange for each shareholder to wire the subscribed capital into this account; the remittance must state the company name, share number, and subscription purpose. Any inbound remittance from a foreign shareholder must clear the bank's foreign exchange declaration and preserve the SWIFT remittance receipt. The bank will provide a statement of deposit balance. The applying certified public accountant will review the bank statement, exchange settlement declarations, and shareholder ledger, then issue a formal capital verification certificate dated no earlier than seven days prior to registration filing. This certificate is the statutory precondition for MOEA registration and may not be substituted by a bank balance certificate.
required_dossiers: Bank capital account opening application
Company name reservation certificate
Articles of incorporation approved at first board meeting
Investment Commission approval certificate (where applicable)
Shareholders' stock subscription ledger
CPA capital verification report
Bank deposit certificate and SWIFT payment confirmation for each remittance
Antimoney-laundering declarations for beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank reports currency-in or exchange-control exceptions, provide the underlying stock subscription agreement and investment approval certificate to the bank's compliance desk. If the CPA refuses to issue a clean capital verification because of payment timing, remit any shortfall immediately and have the CPA re-dated the report only after cleared funds are confirmed; late remittances require a supplementary capital verification and must be disclosed as a correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Company Registration Filing with MOEA One-Stop Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services, One-Stop Company Registration Portal, Taiwan R.O.C.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal incorporation application electronically through the MOEA One-Stop Portal. The application must include complete Articles of Incorporation, the name reservation certificate, the capital verification report, and statutory officer appointment records. The system will compute the registration fee at NTD 1,000 plus any capital-based surcharge. The Portal will send an automatic submission receipt; the registry then performs a substantive document review against the Company Act and the regulations for company registration. If all requirements are met, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate. After issuance, the company must within 15 days register with the National Taxation Bureau for a business tax identification number; the Portal enables integrated filing where the tax registration is submitted simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Form 1 company establishment registration application
Company name and business scope reservation certificate
Articles of incorporation in final notarized form
CPA capital verification report
Director and supervisor consent forms and identity documents
Address use authorization for registered office, including building owner consent or lease
First board resolution appointing statutory officers
Remittance and investment approval certificates as applicable
Uniform invoice and business tax registration application (integrated optional component)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA queries or suspends the registration, the company secretary must respond through the Portal within the required statutory window, addressing each clerical discrepancy or missing attachment. Common remedies include correcting the Chinese registered address transliteration, executing supplemental consent forms, or amending the articles to remove non-registrable provisions. Re-file the corrected packet within five business days; the registry will restart review at the point of suspension without losing the original application priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification, Labor Registration, and Post-Incorporation Gazette Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; local municipal labor and business office; Taiwan Company Gazette publication system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the MOEA registration certificate is issued, the company must complete tax registration by filing the business taxpayer registration form, opening the uniform invoice and tax ledger with the assigned Business Tax Identification Number, and registering the employer withholding accounts. The company must also register employees with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the applicable pension fund; a digital/consulting entity requires no industrial manufacturing license. The operative first board resolution already approves banking and statutory appointments, which must be communicated to the tax authority in the statutory forms. Finally, publish the formation notice in the Taiwan Company Gazette through the MOEA e-publication service, and retain the published notice in the corporate records for bank and counterparty due diligence.
required_dossiers: MOEA company registration certificate
Business tax registration application form
Identity and appointment records of responsible person
Lease or ownership certificate for registered office
Labor insurance and pension fund registration forms
First board resolution containing banking and officer authorization
Company seal affidavit or chop registration statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau flags missing pages or ID contradictions, visit the assigned National Taxation Bureau service counter and submit corrected statutory attestation forms along with the MOEA certificate. For labor registration rejections, re-file electronically after resolving the offending worker-schedule detail. Gazette publication errors must be corrected by filing a supplementary legal notice within ten days; no penalty will apply if the correction is effected before the end of the first quarter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure digital creator-advocacy and multi-channel-network (MCN) agency in advertising and content representation under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810; no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical processing, or warehousing plant is established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating permit, factory registration certificate, or manufacturing license is required for the approved business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) has no jurisdiction over digital advertising and talent representation services without fixed industrial emission sources.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Environmental Registration, Full EIA Report, and pollution control permits are all exempt because the business emits no process wastewater, no volatile organic compounds, and generates only ordinary office municipal solid waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no stack emission limits, no wastewater discharge point, no hazardous waste stream, and no volatile organic compound abatement obligations arise from the company's digital operations; however, general office waste must be disposed of through licensed municipal carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial civil-defense fire permits. The company occupies only a standard commercial office, so the ordinary building occupancy certificate and landlord fire-safety certificate for the premises must be retained. No fire safety equipment installation approval, no structural load inspection, and no Taiwan OSHA industrial plant clearance is triggered. Standard employee labor insurance and general workplace occupational safety requirements under Taiwan's Occupational Safety and Health Act still apply to office operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance of Taiwan, Tax Administration (Taxation Ruling Authority) and the regional National Taxation Bureau competent for the registered place of business, together with the Customs Administration under the Ministry of Finance. Online electronic portals: the MOF Tax E-Counter filing portal at https://tax.nat.gov.tw and the Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform at https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign investor establishing a Taiwan joint venture limited company, first obtain any required inward investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs if the investor is a mainland China entity or from the competent authority under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals for other non-resident investors. Then complete incorporation under the Taiwan Company Act with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; the company registration certificate and company registration number (8-digit Unified Serial Number) are issued at that stage, and this Unified Serial Number is the statutory Tax Identification Number for all subsequent tax filings. Within 15 days of commencing business, or as instructed by the local National Taxation Bureau, the company must file a Tax Registration Application with the regional National Taxation Bureau using the Company Registration Certificate, Unified Serial Number, proof of registered address or fixed place of business, the responsible person's identification, governing documents, and investment approval documents. The National Taxation Bureau will activate the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax registration, the Value-added Business Tax registration, and the Uniform Invoice issuance status. Where the entity is a foreign non-resident taxpayer with no fixed place of business in Taiwan but making taxable Taiwan-source supplies, it must appoint a tax representative and complete the simplified VAT registration procedure through the Cross-Border Electronic Services Tax Registration system; a one-time VAT registration number is then assigned for the non-resident e-commerce taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Taiwan-incorporated profit-seeking enterprise is taxed as an entity on its taxable income under the Income Tax Act, and the same entity is a Business Tax operator under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act. No pass-through classification is available for a Taiwan limited liability joint venture.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election, an LLC-style pass-through election, or a hybrid mismatch classification election. Entity-level income taxation is mandatory for a Taiwan company. The only available optional regime is the small-scale business VAT regime for businesses with average monthly sales below the Uniform Invoice threshold, which is not a corporate tax classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax (VAT) under the Business Tax Act of Taiwan
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$40,000 average monthly sales for service businesses and NT$80,000 average monthly sales for goods businesses constitute the statutory starting point of value-added business tax collection; a business whose average monthly sales exceed NT$200,000 must register as a general VAT taxpayer and issue Uniform Invoices at the standard 5% output VAT rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan does not operate a real-time fiscal device clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping system in the style of territorial clearance regimes. Instead, all general VAT taxpayers must issue serially numbered Uniform Invoices for taxable sales; electronic Uniform Invoices must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform through the certified E-Invoice Turnkey API or an approved system interface using the taxpayer's Unified Serial Number, invoice serial number, and buyer carrier identifier. Paper Uniform Invoices must contain the statutory printed serial number and, for E-Invoice receipts, the random anti-counterfeit code and QR-code carrier. The tax authority performs risk-based reconciliation of invoice data, sales declarations, and export records; non-compliance with Uniform Invoice issuance or platform transmission requirements is penalized under the Uniform Invoice Usage Guidelines and the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, a 0% VAT rate applies to goods actually exported from the Taiwan customs territory; goods or services supplied for export or in connection with export trade; international transport services; and services rendered within Taiwan to foreign enterprises or individuals where the service is consumed or economically used wholly outside Taiwan, including qualifying cross-border creator-management, MCN agency, and digital marketing services supplied to non-resident platform entities, provided the service recipient is outside Taiwan and the consideration is paid in foreign currency. For goods exports, the goods must physically leave the Taiwan customs territory. For services, the provider must maintain contracts and performance records evidencing the non-resident status of the recipient, the offshore use of the service, and the settlement of foreign exchange proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Bill of Export) accepted by Taiwan Customs evidencing export of goods
Original or electronic Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Taiwan customs territory
Commercial Invoice and Packing List matching the export declaration and shipment schedule
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Designated Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Service contract, platform payout statement, performance report, and foreign exchange receipt records for zero-rated cross-border MCN agency services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to post-export audit by the National Taxation Bureau and Customs Administration. If the mandatory documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, falsified, or if the export or foreign exchange receipt is not substantiated within the statutory collection period, the 0% rate is revoked, the sale is reclassified as taxable at the standard 5% VAT rate, and the deficient VAT is assessed together with late interest and penalties. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, a taxpayer who underpays or evades business tax by false export claims or unverified zero-rating is subject to a penalty of up to five times the underpaid tax; aggravated cases may be referred for criminal liability under the Tax Collection Act, and the business may be suspended from issuing Uniform Invoices pending rectification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates under a Central-Bank-managed floating exchange-rate regime; the New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is determined by market supply and demand within a managed band, and both current and capital account conversions are legalised by the Foreign Exchange Control Act. Current account receipts and payments used for the MCN agency's content production, creator payouts, and global talent representation are freely convertible through authorised banks as long as an accurate declaration is filed and the underlying commercial invoice exists. Capital account flows—especially the inward equity injection from the PRC parent—are not free: the Investment Commission under the Ministry of Economic Affairs must pre-approve the Sino-Foreign JV's creation and additional capital calls, and the CBC's authorised bank requires a purpose code and the approval reference to be printed in the SWIFT narrative before funds are credited. Profit remittance hurdles include audited financial statements, a corporate income tax offset/payment clearance certificate, and the preparation of Form of Overseas Remittance for Profit (or equivalent CBC declaration) demonstrating that the cumulative registered capital has been fully paid and capital verification completed. For exports of intellectual property or creator-management revenues, the CBC requires surrender of foreign-currency proceeds into TWD within ten business days after the receipt is posted; however, companies with live trade hedging demands may apply for a foreign-currency retention quota. Failure to surrender on time or speculative round-tripping will attract central-bank penalties and injure the account relationship.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must submit a Report of Foreign Exchange Settlement for Export Proceeds to an authorized bank within 10 working days of receipt of the overseas payment; the standard surrender ratio is 100% conversion into New Taiwan Dollars. Retention in foreign currency is conditionally allowed only if the exporter has a pre-approved CBC foreign-currency deposit balance quota for trade hedging.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency Deposit + NTD Settlement Account)
Capital Escrow Account (NTD + Foreign Currency Deposit)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Taiwan reserves foreign-exchange settlement authority to domestic banks and post offices; the CBC does not permit unlicensed offshore digital EMIs to open local currency clearing accounts or directly service a Taiwan-registered company as a principal bank. Wise B2B and TikTok Creator Payout may only operate as downstream payment indicators if the ultimate settlement is wired to the JV's domestic NTD designated account through a corresponding bank. Fintech EMIs cannot provide the statutory capital verification report, CBC export declaration, or Investment Commission approval receipts required for regulatory filings.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is mandatory for initial onboarding. At least one statutory director and the ultimate beneficial owner must appear in person at the local branch for the first KYC interview; the branch automatically declines remote-only onboarding from PRC-incorporated intermediate vehicles. A notarized power of attorney granted to a Taiwan resident manager may complete periodic reviews after the first physical file, and remote video interviews can be used for supplementary verification if the original passports are verified at the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the PRC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PRC-parent/JV ownership chain appears as a cross-strait direct investment without MOEA Investment Commission approval.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approval letter from the Investment Commission (Ministry of Economic Affairs); the JV's Articles of Incorporation filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; certified copies of the PRC parent's Business License and Articles of Association; a notarized UBO org chart with identity documents for all shareholders holding at least 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: MCN agency fees to a centralised advertising group are deemed potential profit shifting or disguised royalty to the PRC parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fully executed creator representation agreement for each managed influencer; TikTok brand partnership contracts and performance-reporting invoices; Creator Payout statements from TikTok matching the declared 30-70% commission split; contemporaneous meeting minutes documenting service delivery and a transfer-pricing study supporting a remote management fee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency payouts to dozens of local streamers are flagged as layering or unexplained third-party settlement risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A real-name ledger of every contracted creator with government-issued ID, bank letter for payout accounts, and platform order settlement files; a monthly payout reconciliation showing each creator's earnings calculation; signed model releases and content campaigns; an independent AML control assessment of the payment process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection is considered suspicious for failing the capital verification evidence test.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The inbound SWIFT MT103 with the Investment Commission approval number referenced; the CBC foreign exchange declaration form stamped by the receiving authorized bank; the appointed CPA's capital verification report; the original foreign-currency transfer instruction from the PRC parent's bank evidencing documented funding sources.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be remitted by the PRC parent using SWIFT MT103/202 to the JV's designated capital escrow account at a Tier-1 domestic bank, with narrative including the Investment Commission case number and the CBC purpose code FDIT (Foreign Direct Investment in Taiwan). The receiving bank verifies the remitter is the exact equity holder, debits the funds to an escrow, and releases them to the operating account only after a Taiwan CPA issues the capital verification report and the bank confirms the CBC foreign exchange declaration has been filed. Any change in the remitter is refused.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For MCN service commissions paid to overseas streamers, advertising networks and TikTok's Hong Kong payout entity, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 through a domestic Authorized Bank with purpose code Service Charge under CBC rules. For large trade equipment purchases from China, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) or Documentary Collections (MT791) can be used where commercial contracts require a payment guarantee; all outward remittances of profits require an audited balance sheet, tax clearance certificate and CBC profit remittance form.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/TWD forward contracts up to 12 months with documented underlying MCN advertising receivables or creator payout liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to non-TWD exotic currencies where no deliverable forward exists and supporting commercial documentary evidence is held
Cross-currency swaps allowed only for committed medium-term capital loans matched to real operational FX exposure, with CBC declaration and annual risk review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and Board-prepared financial statement submission for shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Department; primary statutory recipient is the shareholders' meeting via the board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the meeting must be held by June 30, with a limited extension to July 15 subject to MOEA approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible person may be fined NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000 for each failure to convene the annual meeting within the statutory window; repeated non-compliance or continued inactivity for more than six months may result in administrative dissolution by the MOEA (strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Annual Income Tax Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (head-office jurisdiction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 1 through May 31 of the year following the taxable year; a one-month extension to June 30 may apply for CPA-prepared returns under prescribed circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 3% per month of the delinquent tax, capped at 30%; late payment surcharge of 1% for every two days, capped at 15%; continued delinquency after enforced collection procedure may lead to cancellation of the company's tax registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after each calendar quarter: April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 for the prior quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine from NTD 300 to NTD 3,000 per return under the Business Tax Act; late payment surcharge of 1% for every two days, up to 15%; repeated non-filing permits the tax authority to revoke the Business Tax registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Company Operating and Financial Performance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (June 30 for a December 31 year-end), ordinarily accompanied by audited financial statements when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may be treated as a breach of foreign investment approval conditions; MOEAIC may suspend or revoke the investment approval and prohibit dividend distributions and capital repatriation until the report is submitted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory CPA audit is mandatory when a non-public company's paid-in capital at fiscal year-end is NTD 30 million or more (approx. USD 970,000), or when annual net operating revenue is NTD 100 million or more (approx. USD 3.23 million). Headcount alone does not impose an independent audit in Taiwan; however, more than 50 employees triggers the obligation to appoint a certified accounting officer under the Business Entity Accounting Act, and more than 200 employees reclassifies the enterprise as a non-small-and-medium enterprise, which may create audit requirements under lender or shareholder covenants. In addition, MOEAIC-approved foreign-invested companies may be contractually or administratively required to file an audited balance sheet and income statement each year even if below the statutory thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies use the Business Entity Accounting Act and the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS), the local GAAP closely aligned with IFRS for SMEs; public companies and companies supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission must use Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS), which is identical to IFRS as endorsed by the FSC. Annual financial statements are denominated in New Taiwan Dollars unless the Investment Commission approves a foreign-currency reporting basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, a Register of Controllers (ultimate beneficial owners) must be maintained at the registered office and filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 15 days after establishment or any change, including any share transfer resulting in a change in control. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation return solely due to the passing of a calendar year; however, the board must verify the continued accuracy of UBO data at each annual shareholders' meeting, and all changes, including a transfer that shifts direct or indirect ownership of more than 10% of voting shares or appoints a new controller, must be reported within the 15-day statutory window. The Register of Members must also be updated immediately upon a share transfer so that the company may lawfully recognize the transferee and enforce pre-emptive rights.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 15,000 per engagement for a mandatory Taiwan CPA audit; USD 3,500 to USD 6,000 for a non-statutory review or compilation
